title: [wall] 2026-11 archive shard crosses the 95 MiB soft ceiling ~2026-11-18 - shard-period/ceiling shape decision owed (F7 of wb-00si L1042)
description:
F7 of wb-00si L1042 (LOW OWNER WEIGH-IN, bound at BIND): the 2026-11 archive shard (52,609,241 B after the L1042 hop) grows ~4.67 MB/day of export growth and crosses the 99,614,720 B soft ceiling ~10 days after the cut (~2026-11-18), BEFORE its month seals on Dec 1. After the ceiling, `tracker-export.mjs compact` exits 2 and every hop refuses (fail closed) - landings stop.

The cure needs a SHAPE decision against owner shape M:61843 ("monthly shards"):
(a) sub-month shard periods (name-form change - owner-scoped),
(b) raise/re-scope the soft ceiling for the current month's shard,
(c) reduce per-close shard bytes (close-reason compaction at the writer - the orchestrator-controllable lever; cand-g1024-exit-close-reason-compactor),
or a combination. Option (c) only slows the horizon; (a)/(b) need the owner.

Horizon math at filing: 99,614,720 - 52,609,241 = 47.0 MB headroom / ~4.67 MB-day = ~10 days. The ceiling guards the main export and EVERY shard (C7/K3 of the compaction suite).
notes:
OWNER RULING 2026-11-08 (relayed by Pi-Subagents Sr. Engineer, msg 1fdee9a6 reply; a refinement of M:61843 element 2, not a reversal) - ADOPT OVERFLOW-CONTINUATION SHARDS:
1. The active month's shard keeps its monthly name until a write would push it past the 95 MiB soft ceiling; the writer then SEALS it immutable mid-month (exactly as at a month seal) and opens the lexicographic continuation issues-closed-YYYY-MM-b.jsonl (then -c, ...). Monthly stays the DEFAULT period; the suffix is the measured-degeneracy response in the small direction, the mirror of the quarter fallback in the large direction. Day shards remain OUT per R-B670.
2. Sealed continuation shards take the same append-only immutability as sealed months.
3. The reader family (the xkto-landed tracker-export readers) extends to glob the suffixed family, with the round-trip selftest extended red-first to a multi-part month including a dep-edge-via-stub across parts.
4. The 95 MiB pre-push guard applies PER SHARD FILE, main included - unchanged.
5. Forward commits only, no history rewrite, fw_commit_locked machine-side.
Ceiling re-scope toward 100 MiB REJECTED (95 is the GitHub-block margin). Rides the normal lane path (~10 days of clock). Close-reason compaction approved as a parallel mitigation.

This bead is now the IMPLEMENTATION bead for elements 1-4 (element 5 is machine-side discipline): writer seal+continuation in qa/workbench/tracker-export.mjs compact, reader glob extension, red-first multi-part round-trip selftest with a dep-edge-via-stub across parts, per-shard guard unchanged.

Use this same text for a K2 first cut and a K4 respin brief. It guides authoring only; it never gates a pick, pauses a lane or changes the gate's TITLE-CENSUS ACCEPTANCE floor. Follow the bead's own acceptance criteria and the independently-authored gate falsifier.

## Pinned reader set

Write the exact pinned reader set before the census: every case by test file path and case id, with its assertion target and observed result. Give the census a title that names that pinned set (the files, cases and observable behavior), not an empty or wider reader category. Each header sentence claims exactly the pinned set it can support. For each positive claim, name the independent falsifier that could turn it red. A failed or missing pin is not a positive claim.

## NOT CLAIMED (scope sentence; no residual semantics; no follow-up bead)

For a mode outside that pinned set, say “<mode> is NOT CLAIMED by this census.” This is a boundary on what the reader proves, not an unresolved test failure, a residual, or a demand to enumerate unrelated modes. No follow-up bead is created from a scope sentence. Do not infer coverage from silence.

## RESIDUAL (named family + pinned quiet row; rule 19(d))

When an escape family within the claimed subject is a real residual, name the family and pin a quiet row: a test that turns red if the quiet page is silenced. Cite that case by file path and case id in the census. Do not label unsupported prose a pinned residual. Keep the FIRST-cut PASS-WITH-FINDING versus refusal distinction of standing rule 19(d): one missing quiet row in an otherwise pinned first-cut enumeration can produce a finding and a follow-up bead; a substantially prose-only enumeration can be refused. The gate still judges independently.

# Narrow census claim form — first cuts and respin briefs

Use this same text for a K2 first cut and a K4 respin brief. It guides authoring only; it never gates a pick, pauses a lane or changes the gate's TITLE-CENSUS ACCEPTANCE floor. Follow the bead's own acceptance criteria and the independently-authored gate falsifier.

## Pinned reader set

Write the exact pinned reader set before the census: every case by test file path and case id, with its assertion target and observed result. Give the census a title that names that pinned set (the files, cases and observable behavior), not an empty or wider reader category. Each header sentence claims exactly the pinned set it can support. For each positive claim, name the independent falsifier that could turn it red. A failed or missing pin is not a positive claim.

Gap (groomed by flywheel seat g2 round 1, run g2-work-r1; measured at origin/workbench/implementation-program b44f1ce): wb-6ze.32 (open, sequenced after wb-6ze.27) files the pure graph-view model src/workbench/graph-view.ts buildGraphView(reader, {scope, focus?, viewport, caps}) with a topologyRevision-keyed model cache and counted supernode collapse; its falsifier F3 pins that an unchanged topologyRevision re-reads no relations, but nothing will measure the model's cost at the W21 grouped-10k shape. Every landed or in-flight W21 receipt times something else: wb-9x5.1/wb-9x5.2 (qa/workbench/inspector-grouped-bench.mjs) time layoutInspector navigation/layout/resize over the pre-model graph branch of workflow-inspector.ts, wb-9x5.4 reducer updates and per-view selectors, wb-9x5.3 retained memory, wb-9x5.5 tool reply sizes, wb-9x5.6 cap saturation, wb-9x5.7 buildTimelineLanes, wb-9x5.8 terminal bytes per update. None calls buildGraphView. docs/workbench/10-terminal-inspector.md § "Rendering pipeline" requires "Graph layout cached by topology revision; no force-directed re-layout in render method. For large graphs show aggregate supernodes first." and § "Scalability targets" sets "layout/nav calculation target <=20ms on benchmark host ... don't declare targets met without measured runs"; docs/workbench/14-qa-and-benchmarks.md § "Performance benchmark" requires "p50/p95 layout render/navigate/resize time" and "report measured hardware/toolchain and outliers. No invented pass numbers." The owner's dialog wiring will build the graph model per redraw for the W15-B6 renderer, so its cost at 10k grouped operations would land on the redraw path unmeasured.

Scope (atomic, measurement-only, hot-file free, no production limit or behaviour change), mirroring wb-9x5.7:
- qa/workbench/graph-view-grouped-bench.mjs (new) over the compiled dist/ (`npm run build` first), reusing buildGroupedFixture, BENCH_ONLY_LIMITS, W21_SHAPE, NAVIGATION_TARGET_MS, assessFixtureShape and GROUPED_FIXTURE_DEFAULTS plus the $W21_SEED/$W21_NODES/$W21_DEPTH/$W21_TICKS overrides from qa/workbench/grouped-fixture.mjs exactly as inspector-grouped-bench.mjs does (never fork a second fixture; never modify grouped-fixture.mjs semantics or exports).
- Two passes over the same fixture: pass "maxQuery-40" with BENCH_ONLY_LIMITS as defined and pass "maxQuery-100" with {...BENCH_ONLY_LIMITS, maxQuery: 100} spread locally in the bench (bench-only; never written into src/). Per pass, sample buildGraphView in three regimes: cold build (fresh cache) per focus node stepping through the fixture invocation in pages of 100 at viewport {30, 100} rows; cache hit (same topologyRevision, same request) immediately after each cold build; single-neighborhood change (one added observed edge bumps topologyRevision, then rebuild for the same focus); >= 1,000 samples per regime per pass; a counting reader wrapper records relations/relationsPage calls per build.
- Receipt (contract 'workbench.graph-view-grouped-bench/v1', one JSON line printed BEFORE the exit code is set, also written to $W21_GRAPH_RECEIPT when set): utc, revision ($W21_REVISION else "working-tree"), node/arch/platform/cpus, fixture shape {seed, nodes, depth, ticks, realised}, per pass and regime: build p50/p95/max ms, relation reads per build p50/max and the count of cache-hit builds whose reads exceeded 0 (must be 0), supernode entries per model p50/max, reference entries per model max, counted partial-label rate per model; outliers: the 5 slowest samples with their request parameters; pass flag.
- Exit codes mirror inspector-grouped-bench.mjs: 0 measured at W21 shape with every judged p95 <= NAVIGATION_TARGET_MS (20) and zero cache-hit reads; 1 measured but a judged p95 over target or a cache-hit read count above 0 (a finding, recorded, never tuned away); 2 the measurement is not the W21 claim (fixture shape not realised, e.g. $W21_NODES below 10,000, or sampling below 1,000); 3 nothing measured (exception on stderr, no receipt).
- test/workbench-graph-view-grouped-bench.test.ts (new, red-first): receipt assessor (field completeness, exit semantics incl. exit 2 on a fast off-shape receipt and exit 1 on a pass claiming over target or a nonzero cache-hit read), the sampled function is the dist buildGraphView (no Date.now/Math.random inside the timed region other than performance.now around the call), production caps unchanged (observation.ts MAX_DEFAULT and the landed graph-view caps pinned; test/workbench-grouped-fixture.test.ts production-cap precedent cited by wb-9x5.7), Forge registration present.
- forge.toml: ONE additive block `[build.commands.graph-view-grouped-bench]` command "node qa/workbench/graph-view-grouped-bench.mjs" timeout 300, outside the default gate list.

Files: qa/workbench/graph-view-grouped-bench.mjs (new), test/workbench-graph-view-grouped-bench.test.ts (new), forge.toml (one command block). Out of scope: src/workbench/graph-view.ts, src/workbench/observation.ts, src/ui/workflow-inspector.ts, qa/workbench/inspector-grouped-bench.mjs, qa/workbench/grouped-fixture.mjs, any production cap or default, wb-9x5.4's reducer/selector sampling, any terminal rendering or redraw claim (wb-9x5.8).
acceptance_criteria:
1. docs/workbench/14-qa-and-benchmarks.md § "Performance benchmark" ("p50/p95 layout render/navigate/resize time"; "report measured hardware/toolchain and outliers. No invented pass numbers."): the receipt carries build p50/p95/max per pass (maxQuery-40, maxQuery-100) and regime (cold, cache-hit, neighborhood-change), node/arch/platform/cpus, revision, fixture shape and the 5 slowest samples with request parameters; a receipt missing any field is assessed exit 2 by the test.
2. docs/workbench/10-terminal-inspector.md § "Rendering pipeline" ("Graph layout cached by topology revision"): the count of cache-hit builds whose relation reads exceeded 0 is recorded and must be 0 for exit 0; a nonzero count exits 1 as a recorded finding, never tuned away.
3. docs/workbench/10 § "Scalability targets" ("don't declare targets met without measured runs"): exit 0 only when the W21 shape was realised (>= 10,000 nodes, >= 1,000 samples per regime) and every judged p95 <= NAVIGATION_TARGET_MS; a fast but off-shape run exits 2; the test pins both outcomes on synthetic receipts.
4. Supernode and reference honesty: per model the receipt records supernode entries p50/max, reference entries max and the counted partial-label rate at maxQuery 40 and 100; the maxQuery-100 pass is a local spread of BENCH_ONLY_LIMITS, and the test pins that production caps and defaults in src/ are unchanged.
5. The sampled function is the compiled dist buildGraphView with performance.now around the call only; grouped-fixture.mjs is imported, never modified; forge.toml gains exactly one command block outside the default gate; no src/ edit anywhere on the branch.
6. Delivery note tables the measured numbers with the host description and exit code actually produced; an exit 1 is reported as a finding, not fixed by changing limits.
